text:
Alex: Heads up — nightly kbench flagged ~12% p50 latency regression on Ampere (p4) for seqlen=1024 compared to yesterday. CC perf team.
Maria: ugh, any diffs in kernel pick/autotune since last good run?
Chen: yes, autotune bumped the default kv-prefill kernel to krnl_v2 for midseq paths yesterday at 03:10 UTC. I have a quick diff.
perf-ci-bot: nightly-kbench: Ampere p4 seqlen=1024 p50: 34.2ms (was 30.3ms) — delta +12.9%. test: kbench/candidate-suite/nightly. artifacts: s3://redwood-ci/kbench/1758884321/report.html
Alex: thanks. Maria, can you pull that report and grep the kernel names and batch sizes?
Maria: pulling now. quick snippet: `grep -A2 "seqlen=1024" report.html | sed -n '1,40p'`
Maria: report shows kernel picks: krnl_v2 for kv-prefill, krnl_v1 for attn-main; batch sizes avg 2.1 (continuous batching)
Chen: krnl_v2 has a different prefetch ordering that regresses long-seqlen on Ampere in microbench I saw earlier but masked by kv-warmup previously. KV cache warmup pattern changed after the prefill reorder.
Sam: can we repro locally? I can run the microbench harness with exact workload. Command I'll run:

```
./kbench --arch ampere --seqlen 1024 --model gpt-small --kernels krnl_v1,krnl_v2 --iters 200 --batch-policy continuous --kv-prefill 1
```

Sam: will also capture perf counters (L1/L2 miss) and kv-hit timeline.
Jess: note that prod routing started sending a small percentage to this pick (canary) at 04:00 UTC — might explain customer-facing impact.
Alex: good catch. If microbench reproduces, we need a quick rollback of the autotune pick or a targeted gating rule for Ampere+seqlen>=1024.
perf-ci-bot: queued a focused microbench job on ampere with artifacts -> job id 1758884380 (running).
Chen: I have a patch to make prefetch ordering conditional on seqlen > 512. Quick diff: `if (seqlen>512) use_prefetch_order(old) else use_prefetch_order(new)` — might be safe.
Maria: before we patch, Sam — can you collect `kv-cache` warmup curves from the harness? I want to compare hit rates across krnl_v1 vs v2.
Sam: grabbing now, attaching a tiny CSV excerpt:
```
# time_ms,kv_hits,kv_lookups
0,0,0
5,12,50
10,40,50
20,48,50
50,50,50
```
Sam: v2 shows slower ramp to full hits for seqlen=1024 vs v1 (v1 hits ~90% by 10ms, v2 ~60%).
Chen: that matches the hypothesis — prefetch reorder delays first-page fill for kv shards leading to extra NVMe/GPU roundtrips.
Jess: ops: can infra throttle the canary? We should reduce traffic to that kernel while triage happens. @infra-bot any quick toggle?
infra-bot: Feature-flag update: reduced routing percent for kernel krnl_v2 -> 0.5% (was 5%). change id ff-1758884420.
Alex: plan: 1) Sam runs extended microbench + perf counters (ETA 30m). 2) Chen prepares a minimal revert/guard (prefetch conditional) and unit tests. 3) Maria runs the gating job once microbench confirms. 4) infra keeps canary throttled.
Sam: started extended run (2000 iters), sending perf flamegraph + counter dump to s3://redwood-ci/kbench/1758884321/full.tar.gz. ETA ~25m.
Chen: prepping PR now with tests. I'll mark it as hotfix candidate if microbench reproduces.
Maria: opening an incident channel in #incidents for customer-facing alerts and linking this thread.
Alex: thanks team. Keep updates here only for triage notes; escalate to incident if customer errors rise. :thumbsup:
perf-ci-bot: microbench job 1758884380 completed: regression reproduced; flamegraph link s3://redwood-ci/kbench/1758884321/flame.html
Sam: confirmed counters show higher L2 miss rate during first 15ms for krnl_v2. Attaching short snapshot in the artifact.
Chen: PR #2921 created with conditional prefetch and microbench perf numbers in the description.
Maria: I'll run the gating job after we land the PR; if green, we'll rollout a canary sweep.
Alex: ordering for rollback if gating fails: revert autotune pick + bump routing back to krnl_v1 for Ampere seqlen>=1024. Sam, please post final log when run completes.
Sam: will do. current run finishing, uploading now.
Jess: thumbs up. pinging customer success to inform major customers as precaution.
Alex: great work — short-lived but visible regression. Postmortem if rollback needed.
